---- Draft answers (for SIG section 5) ----
1) In-transit encryption:
- Public API endpoints: TLS 1.3 is enforced for all public-facing endpoints. We support TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 for legacy clients, but TLS 1.2 is permitted only with secure cipher suites; active enforcement of TLS 1.3 is in place for new sessions.
- Private peering / Dedicated / VPC: Mutual TLS (mTLS) is supported and recommended for VPC private peering. We also support IP allowlists and private endpoint connections.
- Cipher suites: AEAD suites only (e.g., TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384).

2) At-rest encryption and envelope model:
- All customer data at rest is encrypted using AES-256-GCM. We use an envelope encryption model: data is encrypted with per-record data keys (DEKs) using AES-256-GCM; DEKs are themselves encrypted with a Key Encryption Key (KEK) managed in our KMS.
- DEKs are ephemeral and cached in the runtime’s secure memory (no long-term plaintext storage). Re-keying of DEKs occurs on object write/update depending on workload; we do not persist raw DEKs to disk.

3) KMS / HSM details:
- Hosted: We use cloud provider KMS (HSM-backed key material) for KEK storage; customer data keys are wrapped/unwrapped by KMS on demand. HSM attestation documents (third-party attestation of the KMS HSM) can be provided for compliance — see attached hsm_audit_certificate_2025.pdf.
- Dedicated / Private: Customers may opt for BYOK (Bring Your Own Key). For BYOK, customers can supply keys stored in their own KMS/HSM; we operate with a customer-managed key policy and perform only wrapping operations as authorized.

4) Key rotation cadence and evidence:
- KEK rotation: Keystores rotate KEKs on a 90-day schedule by default; emergency rotation procedures are documented in the runbook.
- Data key (DEK) rotation: DEKs are rotated per-write; for long-lived objects we schedule re-encryption windows (we support bulk re-encryption jobs with idempotent semantics).
- Rotation evidence: rotation events are logged to our audit pipeline (immutable logs with hash chaining) and retained per account for 2 years. We can export a rotation matrix/csv of recent KEK rotation events (attached: kek_rotation_log_2026Q3.csv).

5) Operational controls / access:
- KEKs are only accessible by a limited set of service accounts bound to the runtime; access is controlled via IAM roles and enforced with short-lived tokens.
- We use HSM-backed key storage on provider KMS; private deployments can integrate with customer HSMs.

Artifacts to attach: 1) redwood_sig_encryption_answers.pdf (consolidated SIG section answers) 2) kek_rotation_log_2026Q3.csv (rotation matrix) 3) hsm_audit_certificate_2025.pdf (attestation)

Notes / caveats:
- For on-prem air-gapped deployments we provide an operator package; HSM integration steps vary by vendor.
- We will mark any Hosted-only statements clearly in the final PDF.
